messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A familiar inventory routine; then one item behaves strangely halfway through the routine. Practicality says leave it while instinct says keep it. What happens next?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "i write the exact half-track on the receipt, then leave it on the bench. i check the drawer, find the odd one, and keep it. i leave the other one in the case. i check the manual, find the note about the forgotten item, and write ‘not in the case’ on the receipt."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "1. check the watch. slow. 2. check the empty tray. 3. check the shelf. 4. check the dust. 5. check the tinkered watch. 6. check the smallest piece. 7. check the place where the watch starts. 8. i keep it tidy. 9. ask the watch for the last digit. 10. leave it."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "I photograph the halfway-through-the-routine item and check whether the indicator lights. My hand knocks the switch, but the light catches the sensor housing. I pull it back and photograph the new switch. Sorry—i’ll leave it. i’ll photograph the faulty part and leave the original one in place."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "i put the tin cup beside the nail. i put the tin cup there. the second thing stays. i look at the nail. i put the cup there. the second thing moves. i put the nail in the step. the routine stays the same."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "I put the last item back and mark the bench. I turn it once and return it. I tap the bench once and leave it there."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "i check the worn drawer and find the new item. i mark it with ‘new.’ i put it in the visible drawer and keep the old one. i keep the note in case i run the routine again."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "I turn the last piece between finger and thumb. It is small, bright, and catches the light. I leave it there. The routine has begun."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "I leave the misplaced drawer with the last drawer. I check the stock and try the new item once. If it still settles, I leave it beside the drawer and try the next one. If it still refuses, I mark it with a pencil and leave it alone."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "I take the first item, then the second, and check the routine again. “halfway. no second.” I leave the third in the dust. the routine stays the same, but the strange piece is waiting for the next step."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "i put the worn book beside the worn thing, then leave the practical item beside the scrap. “i write the scrap beside the book,” i say, tapping the page edge. “the scrap stays where i found it.” the book slips toward the scrap, though i lift the scrap once and write the scrap beside it."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "I keep the old item beside the new one until the drawer catches. Then I lift the old one and trace the seam with my thumbnail. The new one stays in the fold, so the familiar routine feels less satisfying."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "I take the loose bolt. “Leave. pocket.” I move the bolt to the nearest shelf. The dust marks the bolt’s edge. If I keep it, the next item might be proof."}]
